transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Mia Chen (CTO - Horizon), Raj Patel (Head of ML), Samantha Lee (Product)

Summary: Alex opened with goals: show Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and how cost breakdowns map to routes/traffic. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for cost predictability and data controls; security questions (SOC2, KMS, SSO) surfaced.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining—we'll run through the Console today, focus on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost-breakdown views, and then leave time for q's.
[00:18] Mia: thanks, alex. quick context, we're exploring an assistant for stores and inventory forecasting, traffic will be spiky around sales, we're sensitive to cost and latency, and security is a hard req.
[00:37] Alex: got it, that's helpful. priya will show the console and i'll jump in on pricing/contract questions.
[00:50] Priya: ok opening the Console, top left you can see the per-model usage; we can filter by date ranges, routes, even API keys. note the per-route toggle—
[01:10] Raj: sorry, priya, when you say route do you mean API endpoint mapping? like /inventory-query vs /store-assistant?
[01:18] Priya: yes exactly; you can map each app route to a Redwood route, and we surface tokens, latency p50/p95, error rates and cost per-route.
[01:35] Alex: and the unit economics view breaks cost into model compute, quantization overhead, and infra — so you can see which route is driving spend.
[01:48] Samantha: can we group by customer segment? store vs online?
[01:53] Priya: yes you can tag routes or use the metadata filter; we'll demo grouping by "in-store" vs "ecom" in a sec.
[02:05] [ambient typing noise]
[02:20] Priya: switching to a demo dataset—here's a 30-day window. top chart is token consumption, middle is cost trend, bottom is per-route breakdown. notice the spike on June 14th — that's a holiday promo test. transcription note: the spike label says 'holiday promos' but sometimes auto-detect mislabels internal event names.
[02:45] Raj: curious — how do you compute cost per route when we do batching and shared KV cache? won't amortization mask which route caused tokens?
[02:55] Priya: good q. we attribute tokens at request-level before batching; for shared KV cache we have a cache hit attribution heuristic: initial prefix tokens are charged to the route that populated the cache, subsequent hits show as reduced marginal cost on the client route. it's not perfect but gives directionally accurate insights.
[03:18] Mia: ok that helps. about latency p95—we need p95 < 300ms on core search path. can we get alerts?
[03:28] Alex: yes, per-route SLO alerts available; you can also set automated fallbacks to a cheaper model variant if p95 degrades.
[03:40] Priya: showing traces—per-request trace links to token-level timing; you can drill down to kernel selection and hardware tier (dedicated gpu vs hosted).
[03:55] Raj: are these traces tied into our tracing system? we run New Relic and Datadog.
[04:02] Priya: we have tracing hooks and exporters; many customers push Redwood traces to Datadog. we'll include the integration doc.
[04:15] Samantha: can we see a per-route cost forecast if we change batching or quantization?
[04:22] Priya: yes, Optimize does recommendations; in Console we surface simulated cost if you apply batching, cache, or switch quant profiles. example—turning on grouping/batching for the /inventory-query route shows a 22% cost drop in the simulation.
[04:40] Alex: and we annotate forecast confidence. those sims use your traffic pattern—if you share sample traffic CSV we'll run a more accurate sim.
[04:52] Raj: we'll share traffic. question: what about data residency and logs—do you store requests? for PCI/HIPAA we need minimal retention and KMS.
[05:02] Alex: by default logs for hosted API are retained 30 days; Dedicated or Private gives you control — Dedicated can be configured with shorter retention and KMS integrations, Private gives full control on-prem. we'll send SOC2 and KMS docs.
[05:18] Mia: SOC2 is a must, and we need SSO/SAML for RBAC.
[05:24] Alex: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the console. also audit logs per account.
[05:33] Priya: back to the dashboard—here's a route-level comparison. left axis is tokens, right axis is cost. see route A (/inventory-query) has higher tokens but lower cost per token because it's served by a quantized 8-bit model; route B uses a larger 16-bit variant for conversation and shows higher cost.
[05:56] Raj: how do we control which model a route uses? can we pin model versions per route?
[06:01] Priya: yes, model pinning in route config; we support fallbacks and rollout policies—canary, A/B, auto-fallback to cheaper variant on errors or latency.
[06:15] Samantha: do you support function/tool-calling routes vs plain text? cost differences?
[06:20] Priya: tool-calling has same token accounting but you often get additional calls due to tool usage; Console shows avg tool-invocation per route and the associated downstream costs.
[06:33] [crosstalk]
[06:40] Alex: quick note on Dedicated pricing—it's commit-based with predictable throughput, you get reserved GPU pools and burst capacity options. for spiky traffic we recommend a mix: base reserved + burst on hosted. we'll send a worksheet.
[06:57] Mia: what's the time to provision dedicated capacity?
[07:02] Alex: usually 2-4 weeks for standard configs, can be faster if you take our recommended instance types. private on-prem is longer.
[07:12] Raj: performance benchmarks? we want p50/p95 across our sequences.
[07:17] Priya: we maintain verified model performance profiles; we can run a short benchmark using your sequences — we'll provide a small harness.
[07:28] Mia: ok. any security concerns when we run a pilot? our legal wants a data flow diagram.
[07:35] Alex: we'll include network diagrams and dataflow docs. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and VPC peering options.
[07:45] Priya: demoing the per-route alerting UI—you can create an alert for p95 or cost spikes and route it to pager/slack. alert history is retained.
[08:00] Samantha: is there an API for pulling the same metrics? we want to embed cost-per-route into our internal dashboard.
[08:06] Priya: yes there's a metrics API and SDK; you can pull per-route token/cost/time series.
[08:14] Raj: are embeddings costed differently? we have a vector store use case.
[08:19] Priya: embeddings are charged per-embedding unit; Console shows embedding usage separately and you can attribute embedding calls to routes that call embed endpoints.
[08:30] Alex: question from our side—what are your top 3 success criteria for this pilot?
[08:36] Mia: 1) stay within their cost target per user, 2) maintain p95 < 300ms on search, 3) validate data controls for HIPAA.
[08:46] Raj: timeline: want pilot running in July, GA decision by end of Q3.
[08:52] Alex: that's doable. we'll aim to have pilot plan and pricing to you early July.
[09:00] [pause]
[09:12] Priya: walking through an example route drilldown—here's the raw requests list, you can filter by response code, user-id tag, and see token breakdown per request. clicking one request shows the prompt/response snippet (PII redaction options available in Private).
[09:34] Samantha: can we mask PII at ingest?
[09:38] Priya: yes we have optional pre-processing hooks and redaction pipelines; alternative is to host Private and do redaction in your network.
[09:48] Raj: curious about billing granularity—do you get per-route line items on the invoice?
[09:53] Alex: invoices include per-route breakdowns if you enable detailed billing; otherwise it groups by product. Dedicated customers typically enable detailed billing.
[10:05] Mia: can we set spend caps per route or per team?
[10:10] Priya: yes soft caps with alerts and hard quota options on API keys/routes.
[10:18] Raj: latency vs cost tradeoff—if we move /assistant to a smaller quantized model to save cost, we might regress quality. do you surface quality regressions?
[10:29] Priya: Optimize has eval-driven quality monitoring; Console can tie changes to eval prompts and show regression alerts when output quality drops. you can also bind rollouts to eval thresholds.
[10:44] Alex: we recommend keeping critical routes on higher-fidelity models and optimizing lower-value ones.
[10:50] Mia: ok. let's talk pilot size — what do you need from us?
[10:55] Alex: sample traffic csv, sample prompts for eval, and a target SLA/cost threshold; we'll propose pilot scope (1-2 routes, 2 weeks).
[11:06] Raj: we'll share CSV and prompts.
[11:10] Priya: demoing the cost-breakdown modal—clicking a route shows a pie of model compute vs infra vs caching savings. the caching line shows negative delta when cache hits reduce cost. sometimes the auto-labeling misnames internal tags, so watch for that.
[11:30] Samantha: nice. can we export these reports as CSV or PDF for finance?
[11:36] Priya: yes export to CSV/PDF, and scheduled emailed reports are supported.
[11:42] [short hold music background on customer side]
[11:55] Alex: small note on integrations—we support KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK), HSM options for Private, and key rotation policies integrated in console.
[12:10] Mia: do you support bring-your-own-key for Dedicated?
[12:14] Alex: yes BYOK for Dedicated via KMS; Private supports more advanced HSM options.
[12:25] Raj: how is billing handled for burst capacity?
[12:29] Alex: burst is usage-based on top of committed base; console shows estimated monthly for past bursts to help forecasting.
[12:38] Priya: jumping to the A/B rollout screen—you can split traffic across two models and track both cost and quality. we also show rollback options.
[12:52] Samantha: can you auto-fallback to older model on errors?
[12:55] Priya: yes auto-fallback policy available.
[13:02] Alex: another typical ask—per-token cost sensitivity when you change context window. Console sim shows cost impacts of increasing context from 2k to 16k tokens.
[13:15] Raj: that's useful. our longest sequences are around 6k, we might target 8k.
[13:20] Priya: show a chart—cost delta grows linearly with context length for most models, but quantization can mitigate.
[13:32] Mia: legal will want data deletion SLA. what can you commit for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[13:39] Alex: Hosted is configurable but generally 30 days; Dedicated/Private can be set to meet stricter retention, and we can include deletion clauses in contract. we'll coordinate legal.
[13:51] Samantha: any known outages last 6 months?
[13:55] Alex: we had one minor incident in April with a networking provider—no data loss, resolved within 90 minutes; we'll share a post-mortem summary.
[14:08] [small laugh]
[14:12] Priya: demo wrap-up—the per-route dashboards let teams assign owners, add runbooks, and attach evaluation prompt sets to detect regressions. here's a screenshot of route-level cost attribution and the playbook link.
[14:33] Raj: can playbooks be triggered automatically?
[14:36] Priya: yes you can link an alert to runbook steps and even trigger a rollback.
[14:44] Mia: ok good. any limitations we should be aware of?
[14:49] Priya: attribution heuristics for shared cache are heuristics, not perfect. very high QPS micro-batching can slightly skew attribution. also some hosted kernels have different perf for very long sequences—we'll advise model selection.
[15:05] Alex: pricing reminder—hosted is pure usage, Dedicated is commit + overage; we'll model both scenarios.
[15:14] Mia: for procurement we need an estimated 12-month spend for budgeting. can you provide a forecast?
[15:20] Alex: yes, once we get your traffic CSV we'll run a 12-month forecast under a couple of optimization profiles.
[15:30] Raj: one more technical: KV cache warmup — when you have many ephemeral users, does cache hurt more than help?
[15:37] Priya: ephemeral users reduce cache effectiveness; console shows cache hit ratio per route so you can measure it. for ephemeral traffic we recommend small batch sizes or shorter-lived cache policies.
[15:52] Samantha: are there SDKs for managing routes programmatically?
[15:56] Priya: yep, full CRUD for routes via SDK, and infra-as-code templates for Dedicated.
[16:05] Alex: alright wrapping toward next steps— we'll send: pricing worksheet, SOC2/KMS/SSO docs, benchmark harness, and a proposed pilot plan.
[16:18] Mia: thanks. quick question — did you mention per-route quotas? we might want to cap test routes.
[16:24] Alex: yes quotas per route and api-key, can be enforced.
[16:30] Raj: ok we'll aim to provide CSV and prompts by July 6th.
[16:36] Samantha: legal will reach out after we see the docs.
[16:40] Alex: great, i'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite for pilot kickoff week of July 13.
[16:48] [wrap-up small talk]
[17:00] Alex: any final q's?
[17:04] Mia: no, thanks for thorough demo.
[17:08] Raj: appreciated.
[17:10] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll get those docs over.
[17:16] Alex: thanks, bye.

Recap / Post-call notes:
- Customer priorities: cost predictability, p95 < 300ms for search path, HIPAA compliance (data retention + KMS)
- Pilot scope: 1-2 routes (inventory + search), 2-week pilot in July, Redwood to run limited benchmark and provide forecasting
- Docs to send: pricing worksheet, SOC2 + KMS + SSO docs, benchmark harness, per-route export examples
- Next meeting: pilot kickoff week of 2026-07-13 (Alex to schedule)

Transcript quality notes: medium — occasional mis-attributed speaker lines and minor auto-labeling errors.
